1) 从告警标签取 name（Connector 名），用 jstack \u0: 1) Take name (the connector name) from the alert labels, capture thread stacks with jstack <pid>, and count which method the http-nio-* threads are stuck in; 2) Many threads blocked on the database or an outbound HTTP call means a slow downstream: fix it and add timeouts to the call; 3) As a stopgap raise maxThreads for that connector in server.xml, re-checking memory and the downstream capacity; 4) Longer term add circuit breaking around external dependencies (for example Resilience4j) so downstream flapping cannot saturate the Tomcat thread pool.
1) 在 access log 的 pattern 里确认已带 %D，执行 aw: 1) Confirm the access log pattern includes %D, then run awk '{print $NF, $7}' localhost_access_log.*.txt | sort -rn | head -20 to find the slowest URLs; 2) Capture jstack <pid> three times in a row and diff them to find methods that persist across captures; 3) If threads are stuck on the database, check slow queries and connection pool waits (threads block in getConnection when the pool is exhausted); 4) If they are stuck in GC, confirm the Full GC frequency with jstat -gcutil <pid> 1s and then resize the heap or hunt the memory leak based on heap usage.
1) 执行 grep -E ' (5[0-9]{2}|4[0-9]{2}) ': 1) Run grep -E ' (5[0-9]{2}|4[0-9]{2}) ' logs/localhost_access_log.*.txt | awk '{print $7}' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head to find the URLs where the errors concentrate; 2) For 5xx, look for the matching exception stack in logs/catalina.out and the application logs; 3) 4xx concentrated on a few endpoints usually means a caller changed parameters or authentication; confirm with the calling team; 4) If the errors come from dependency timeouts, add timeouts and fallbacks to those calls first so the errors stop amplifying.
1) 执行 jstat -gcold \u003cpid\u003e 1s 10: 1) Run jstat -gcold <pid> 1s 10 and watch whether the old generation drops after each Full GC; 2) If it does not, run jmap -histo:live <pid> | head -30 to find the largest object types; 3) The usual leak sources are static collections, uncleaned ThreadLocals, and class loader leaks from repeated hot deployments; jcmd <pid> GC.class_stats helps confirm; 4) Once a leak is ruled out, consider raising -Xmx or switching to G1 and tuning -XX:MaxGCPauseMillis.
1) 执行 jstat -gcutil \u003cpid\u003e 1s 1: 1) Run jstat -gcutil <pid> 1s 10 and watch the Full GC frequency and the old-generation occupancy after collection; if it stays high after collection there is a leak; 2) Run jmap -histo:live <pid> | head -30 to rank objects and identify the class growing abnormally; 3) If you suspect a leak, dump the heap with jmap -dump:live,format=b,file=/tmp/heap.hprof <pid> and analyse the reference chain in MAT; 4) If it is simply undersized, raise -Xmx after checking physical memory, leaving room for off-heap memory.
1) 登录主机执行 ps -ef | grep catalina 与 ss -l: 1) Log in to the host and run ps -ef | grep catalina and ss -lntp | grep 8080 to check the process and port; 2) If the process is alive, verify with curl -u <user>:<pass> 'http://127.0.0.1:8080/manager/status?XML=true'; a 401/403 means the manager account or a RemoteAddrValve restriction is blocking the collector's IP; 3) If the process is gone, check the tail of logs/catalina.out for the cause (port conflict, insufficient memory, application start-up failure); 4) Confirm the upstream load balancer has removed this node before restarting so traffic stops arriving.
JVM 老年代使用率已超过 90%，说明对象大量晋升且回收不掉，通常是内存泄漏或: JVM old-generation usage has exceeded 90%, meaning objects are being promoted faster than they can be collected. This usually precedes a memory leak or an undersized heap and a Full GC pause can happen at any moment.
Tomcat JVM 堆内存使用率已超过最大堆的 85% 并持续 5 分钟，接下: Tomcat JVM heap usage has exceeded 85% of the maximum heap for 5 minutes. Frequent Full GCs and eventually an OutOfMemoryError are likely next.

该 Connector 的忙碌线程数已超过 maxThreads 的 85%，线: Busy threads on this connector have exceeded 85% of maxThreads. Once threads are exhausted, new requests fall into the acceptCount queue and are rejected outright when that fills.
